A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SparseWorld-TC. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy-forecasting experiments, trajectory and training ablations, per-class results and Gaussian-rendering examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds attention ablations, memory measurements, small-object experiments and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a tested class-reweighted loss variant for small objects. The core architecture, default Chamfer/focal objective and random-ensemble training remain unchanged. Expanded trajectory-embedding and Gaussian-rendering descriptions do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use Occ3D-nuScenes for short- and long-horizon occupancy forecasting and show trajectory-conditioned prediction and sensor rendering. The added analyses examine existing classes and driving conditions without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the camera-based SparseWorld comparator by Dang et al. The OccVAR row is relabeled and cited as OccTENS-F with identical scores; the PDFs do not establish a distinct new evaluation for that row. COME-F becomes COME with its scores retained.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark metrics, horizons and training settings remain unchanged. New appendix experiments introduce frame-wise and simple multi-view aggregation controls, larger configurations with 4800 anchors/64 points or 9600 anchors/16 points, class reweighting and evaluation-memory measurements.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained trajectory, embedding and training-strategy ablations, v3 adds temporal/deformable attention tests, extends anchor/point scaling with memory tradeoffs, and tests small-object improvements. Appendix B also adds refinement visualization and explicit failure-case analysis. These substantially broaden examination of architectural components, scaling and weaknesses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Reported averages across forecast horizons or ray thresholds are not run-level uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched scores in Tables 1–6 are unchanged, and v1 Tables 7–8 become unchanged v3 Tables 10–11. Added results include SparseWorld's 13.20 average mIoU, attention-ablation mIoUs of 25.07 and 23.89, and 30.88 mIoU for the new 9600-anchor variant. These supplement existing results under additional configurations.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.1 newly specifies the affine embedding definition f'' = gamma(fP)·(f + fT) + beta(fP), replacing a verbal description, and explicitly assumes fixed raw sensor frequency. Existing numbered Equations (1)–(6) remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: sparse attention-based forecasting without discrete tokenization or BEV, trajectory conditioning, strong short-term benchmark performance and long-term forecasting capability.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly identifies failures involving heavy occlusion and small objects six seconds ahead. It also states the Gaussian implementation's front-camera restriction and attributes rendering voids to query sparsity. The existing qualification about evaluating multiple possible futures against one ground truth remains.

D1.justification: v3 specifies seven-component waypoint poses, their 16-component relative transformation representation and embedding operations. Appendix B.1 newly discloses rendering resolutions of 256×704 and 128×352 with 7200 anchors and 32 points per anchor. Existing optimizer, hardware, training budget and code link remain; class-reweighting coefficients are unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to SparseWorld and Scaling Up Occupancy-Centric Driving Scene Generation, and cites OccTENS for the relabeled comparison row. SparseOcc's bibliography entry disappears although Appendix A.1 retains its attribution. The broader related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The trajectory-embedding paragraphs are rewritten more precisely, appendix subsections are expanded and reorganized, and author emails and acknowledgments are added. Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 7–9 and Figures 9–10, expands Table 1, relocates the Gaussian examples and renumbers retained appendix displays. Existing qualitative grids receive formatting changes, while the main architectural figures and established result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations, memory/performance comparisons and explicit failure examples improve validation and practical transparency. More precise embedding and rendering details also aid reproducibility. The gains are limited: central benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the new class-reweighting experiment lacks exact weights and uncertainty estimates.
